one_liner: Pentagon analyst for the Air Force's nuclear enterprise: assessing risks, drafting official correspondence, running leadership taskings, and recommending policy actions across mission partners.
fit_summary: The posting requires a year of GS-12-level experience developing and implementing policies for nuclear programs, plus a Top Secret clearance after selection. Daniel's resume has no nuclear or radiological program work, so he is unlikely to qualify even though his coordination and meeting-minutes work fits the correspondence side.
eligibility: Open to the public, so no federal status is needed.

Specialized experience: at least one year at the GS-12 level or equivalent developing and implementing policies that support nuclear programs, including recommending actions on issues that affect the programs' mission.
Top Secret clearance is required; expect a full background investigation if selected.

The posting's wording is ambiguous: it says the GS-12-equivalent experience was gained 'in the federal service' but also credits 'other pay systems,' so it is unclear whether private-sector consulting counts.
Duty station is the Pentagon in Arlington, telework-eligible but not remote; promotion potential is GS-13.
strategy: Skip this one: it requires a year of GS-12-level experience developing and implementing policies for nuclear programs, and his resume shows no nuclear or radiological program work.
Target GS-9 to GS-12 management analyst (0343) roles or FEMA, DHS and Virginia VDEM emergency management roles instead, where his IEM experience maps directly.
resume_bullets: Kept minutes at a large travel company's weekly meetings (Feb – Aug 2024) and at a state health agency's mpox response meetings (2022–2023).
Led a Simulation Cell unit at FEMA full-scale exercises two years in a row.
interview_questions: Describe your experience developing or implementing policy that supported a nuclear or radiological program.
How would you coordinate a tasking response that needs input from several mission partners with conflicting equities?
Walk us through an analysis where you used quantitative methods to compare alternative solutions for leadership.
Tell us about drafting correspondence for senior decision-makers on a tight deadline.
watch_outs: The nuclear-specific specialized experience requirement is the biggest barrier and likely disqualifying without nuclear program work.
A Top Secret clearance is required, which means a lengthy investigation; any clearance issues would end your candidacy.
The GS-13 level expects a full year of GS-12-equivalent experience, which is senior for a first federal job.
